what: Stifel is a mid-sized American investment bank and brokerage. It manages wealth for individuals through thousands of advisers, and advises mid-sized companies on raising capital and selling themselves.
customers: Affluent households through its adviser network, and mid-sized companies needing capital markets advice.
money: the larger part and most of the profit
brokerage, advisory and banking for individuals
moat: Advisers who bring client relationships with them when they join, and a long record of recruiting teams from larger banks that have grown the asset base year after year.
risks: Investment banking fees fall sharply when markets close to new issues
Interest earned on client cash is a large profit source and falls with rates
Recruiting advisers is expensive and the payback takes years
opportunities: 11.9 times earnings with $793M of free cash flow and $2.3B of cash
Revenue grew from $4.7B to $6.3B in four years
Analysts see about 16% upside, and wealth management revenue is far steadier than banking fees
watch: Client assets in wealth management and investment banking revenue.
